research_scope: Source-free, mathematically type-aware audit of shared prerequisites; no source edits and no broad Batch143 population.

aliases.reason: Algebraicity of a field extension invokes a univariate k-polynomial f(T); the general indexed R-polynomial algebra includes the one-variable polynomial ring with R=k. Evaluation at α and nonzero-polynomial requirements are additional parent conditions, not automatically part of the polynomial-ring prerequisite.

The algebraic-extension source selects a nonzero polynomial P∈F[T], which is an element of the one-variable polynomial ring over F. The general indexed polynomial-algebra construction includes this case; the nonzero predicate and existence of a root are retained in the parent definition.

The strongly transcendental source forms finite coefficient polynomial expressions a_0+...+a_n x^n under R⊆S, using the one-variable polynomial-algebra structure over R before evaluation at x∈S. The ambient polynomial ring is the shared prerequisite; evaluation and annihilator implications remain separate.

The affine quasi-coherent sheaf source and the Zariski topology/constructible sources invoke exactly distinguished principal opens D(f) of Spec(R). The localization-of-sections theorem and covers by those opens remain different parent conditions.

A closed immersion of locally ringed spaces asks for a locally section-generated kernel ideal sheaf ker(O_X→i_*O_Z). This is an instance of a locally section-generated ideal subsheaf I⊆O_X used in closed-subspace construction; being specifically a kernel and the immersion's topological conditions remain parent-specific.
